sections.purpose: To measure blood glucose concentration using a portable glucometer as part of clinical pharmacology and pharmacy practice sessions.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacology laboratory for blood glucose monitoring practicals and clinical skills training.
procedure: Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water and dry completely before testing.
Insert a fresh test strip into the glucometer — the device should power on automatically.
Verify the code on the test strip vial matches the code displayed on the glucometer (if applicable to model).
Clean the finger site with 70% isopropyl alcohol and allow to dry completely — do not blow to dry.
Prick the side of the fingertip using a sterile single-use lancet fitted in the lancing device.
Apply gentle pressure at the base of the finger to encourage a small drop of blood — do not squeeze hard.
Wipe away the first drop of blood.
Touch the edge of the test strip (not the top) to the blood drop and allow the strip to absorb the sample.
Wait for the result (typically 5–10 seconds depending on the model).
Read the glucose value displayed on the screen in mg/dL or mmol/L.
Record the value along with time, fasting/postprandial status, and subject details.
Remove and dispose of the test strip and lancet in appropriate waste containers.
Turn off the glucometer if it does not switch off automatically.
Normal fasting blood glucose: 70–100 mg/dL; postprandial (2 hours): <140 mg/dL.
precautions: Use only compatible test strips for the specific glucometer model.
Check expiry date on test strips before use — expired strips give erroneous results.
Store test strips in their original vial with the cap tightly closed; avoid humidity and direct sunlight.
Never reuse lancets — use a fresh sterile lancet for each test.
Ensure the finger site is fully dry after alcohol cleaning before pricking.
Extremely high or low haematocrit can affect readings — note this limitation.
Certain medications (paracetamol, ascorbic acid) may interfere with some glucometer readings.
Calibrate or perform quality control checks with glucometer control solution as per manufacturer's guidelines.
Dispose of lancets in approved sharps containers immediately; dispose of strips as biohazard waste.
